$comment: Cross-engine conformance fixtures for effect combination. SOURCE OF TRUTH: github.com/unveilr/unveilr-guard/conformance/effects.json. Vendored copies elsewhere MUST be byte-identical; each runner asserts the sha256 in README.md.

pairs.name: allow loses to deny
pairs.why: The whole point of forbid-overrides. If this ever inverts, every allow policy becomes a bypass.

pairs.name: combination is commutative
pairs.why: Order of evaluation must not change the outcome, or the decision depends on how policies happened to be loaded.

pairs.name: idempotent
pairs.why: Two rules agreeing must not escalate past what either said.

pairs.name: step_up outranks require_approval
pairs.why: Re-authentication is strictly stronger than a second pair of eyes.

pairs.name: require_approval outranks scoped_token
pairs.why: A narrowed credential still proceeds unattended; an approval does not.

pairs.name: scoped_token outranks sanitize
pairs.why: Constraining authority is stronger than rewriting an argument.

pairs.name: allow with itself stays allow
pairs.why: Guards the inverse failure: a combinator that escalated on agreement would deny everything.

sets.name: one deny in a permissive set
sets.why: Adding a policy must never widen access, regardless of position in the set.

unknownEffects.$comment: Engines DIVERGE here today; see conformance/README.md. These cases are declared, not yet jointly enforced. `expectation` is the agreed target behaviour, `enforcedBy` lists the engines currently asserted against it.
unknownEffects.expectation: fail-closed: an effect absent from `precedence` is treated as at least as restrictive as deny, never discarded

cases.name: unknown vs allow
cases.why: An effect from a newer policy bundle must not be silently dropped in favour of the permissive one.
